title: Fixed term employment - rights compared to permanent employees
p1:
Think a fixed-term employee has fewer workplace rights simply because their contract has an expiry date?

That assumption could cost employers and employees more than they realise.
p2:
A fixed-term employee is hired for a specific period or until a particular project ends. But having an end date does not automatically mean having fewer rights.

In India, fixed-term employees are entitled to wages, working hours, allowances and statutory benefits comparable to permanent employees performing similar work. They are also entitled to proportionate statutory benefits based on their period of service.
p3:
Here is the surprising part: fixed-term employees can qualify for gratuity after completing one year of service under the applicable labour law provisions, unlike the general five-year requirement for permanent employees.

However, fixed-term employment normally ends when the agreed contract period expires. Permanent employment does not operate on the same automatic expiry principle.

The practical takeaway? Employers should not use fixed-term contracts as an excuse to deny statutory benefits or equivalent employment conditions. Employees should carefully check their contract, benefits and applicable labour protections before signing.
conclusion: Do you think fixed-term employees should enjoy exactly the same employment protections as permanent employees, even when their contracts have an expiry date? Share your perspective.
